lots.key_photo_findings: Enlarged crops show deep embossed scroll and cherub borders typical of stamped silver plate or silver-foil over resin; no hallmarks visible on any frame face. The Grosvenor frame still has its shop card insert (Grosvenor is a gift-ware brand name, not a hallmark). Hand mirrors and comb are the common pressed cherub dressing-set pattern. Solid Brass tri-fold frame still has its retail insert. Jewellery box is carved timber with a mirror lid and red flocked lining. No obvious damage seen but the backs are not shown.
lots.condition: Appears clean and unused to lightly used from the single front-on photo. Backs, stands and mirror glass not shown. No hallmarks seen.
lots.question_for_armitage: Do any of the frames, the velvet mirror or the hand mirrors carry a sterling or 925 hallmark on the front edge or back (or are they marked EPNS, silver plated or resin)? Are all the mirror glasses and frame glasses intact, and do the frame stands work?
lots.score_reason: Modern plated or foil gift-shop frames and dressing items routinely hammer $10 to $35 a lot in Tasmania; only a sterling surprise would change that, and nothing in the photo suggests one.

lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1 shows the whole group. Crop shows the ruby decanter is flashed and gilt banded with a cut stopper, gilt wear not visible at this size; the turquoise vase is a swung form with a silver foil label too small to read (could be Italian or US, unknown); the green vase is optic-ribbed swirl glass. Photos 2 and 3 show the milk glass vase with an applied amber trailing vine, a small flake on the inner rim and a brown residue inside. lots.key_photo_findings: Three draped female figures with long hair and fishtail-like lower bodies around a fluted stem ending in acanthus scrolls. Photo 3 shows the silvered finish crazed and lifting on the stem, suggesting silver paint or plating over resin or spelter rather than solid chromed bronze. Base is black painted timber or composite with small edge wear and a chip at the lower left. Amber crackle glass globe appears intact. No maker's mark visible.
